users-answer-better-than-they-write.header: Questions can draw out richer answers
users-answer-better-than-they-write.description: In a study on preference elicitation, users' answers to model questions were often more informative than prompts they wrote unaided, and users reported less effort [1]. This does not show that everyone always answers better, or that the finding applies to every task.

li-eliciting-human-preferences.title: Li et al., Eliciting Human Preferences with Language Models

prompts-generated-from-requirements.description: REprompt builds a multi-agent prompt optimizer from requirements-engineering principles; the abstract reports effective optimization without numbers, and it is an early preprint [1].

shi-reprompt.title: Shi, Sun, Chen, Wu, Chen, Jin, Liu, REprompt: Prompt Generation for Intelligent Software Development Guided by Requirements Engineering

separate-session.title: Separate session
separate-session.script: Meta prompting means using one AI chat to help write a brief for another. Focused questions can draw out details, but the AI should not invent them: if a service check or deadline is unknown, leave it open to confirm. You can review the draft before handing it to the agent.

fresh-chat-clean-work-order.title: Fresh chat, clean work order
fresh-chat-clean-work-order.script: Then take the result into a fresh chat instead of continuing the long one. The bench is where the AI’s context sits, and it gets one clean work order, not the whole conversation that led to it.

why-a-separate-office.title: Why a separate office
why-a-separate-office.script: Why keep a separate planning chat? It can contain questions, half-ideas and drafts that do not all belong in the handover. Take the useful brief into a fresh chat; leave unresolved details clearly marked rather than turning a guess into a fact.
